title: Duke's late-life decline and rehearsing at the 1973 Carnegie concert
summary: Bigard thinks Duke grew senile rather than paranoid; for George Wein's Carnegie Hall reunion he rehearsed 'Rose Room' with Duke, and Ray Nance told him of a threat from Duke's valet.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: He got very paranoid in later years. Was he -- Did he used to be like that? Did he used to --

No. That's what I said. Well, I thought that -- to me he got more senile than anything else, not paranoid, because I've never known him to act like he did on the end of his life there, the way he was doing, the things that he was doing.

And every time I saw him he would want to grab me and hug me, you know. And then the last time -- the time that I was teed off on him was at the concert at Carnegie Hall when he was supposed to introduce some of his past musicians in his band. You know, for the Newport Jazz Festival.
No, '73, I guess it must have been because he died in '74. It must have been 1973.

Well, -- which was George Wein's idea that he'd like to reminisce, you know, get a few of his men that was in the group, like Sonny, Nance, myself, and somebody else, I don't know. And so George told me, "Get here a little early because Duke is coming in early." He had been working somewhere. I don't know, it was somewhere in Jersey somewhere. And he was coming in for a rehearsal with Nance and Sonny and myself. And so I said, "Okay."

So I came in early and there he was. So he started rehearsing things that he had been playing, I mean, probably all that night. So he said, "What you want to do?" I said, "I'll do something simple." He said, "How about 'Tiger Rag'?" I said, "You must be kidding. 'Tiger Rag'. It's hard. I said simple. Don't you know what simple means?" So he said, "What?" I said, "Rose Room." I said, "Everybody knows 'Rose Room.'" So he said, "Okay." He said, "What tempo?" I said, "You know the right tempo," and I gave him the tempo. So I told him what I wanted and his drummer -- you know where he kept the drummer way up on something. And I'd do little diddles after I'd finish the chorus and the drummer was supposed to follow, you know. So I didn't care, so I said, "Okay."

So that night Sonny was there, Ray Nance was all dressed up, bless his soul, and he had his fiddle. And he was talking about -- Ray Nance was talking to me about Duke had did him something and he was threatened by the guy that -- whoever
he had was his boy. I mean, his valet.
At that point it was Jim Lowe?

I don't know who it was -- to beat up Nance and Nance said, "I wished they would. Anyone" -- he and his son. And Duke was in the room getting his legs shaked down by this guy, (Ray so) Nance said, "Yeah, I wish any one of them would come out there."
